questions.prompt: In OpenAI's Agents SDK, is the local context object sent to the model?

options.text: Yes, everything inside it goes into every prompt that the model gets
options.explanation: The docs say the context object is not sent to the LLM.

options.text: No, it is a local object for your code, and the model does not see it
options.explanation: Right. The docs say the context object is not sent to the LLM. It is purely a local object.

options.text: Only when the run has more than one agent in it, and then all of it is sent
options.explanation: The docs do not say this. The context object is local in every run.

questions.prompt: Why did Anthropic's lead research agent save its plan to memory?

options.text: So that the helper agents could edit the plan while they worked on their tasks
options.explanation: The post gives a different reason: the context window may be cut.

options.text: A context window above 200,000 tokens is truncated, so the plan must be saved
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic engineering post says that past 200,000 tokens the context will be truncated, so keeping the plan matters.

options.text: So that the plan could be shown to the user as the final report of the run
options.explanation: The plan was saved to survive truncation, not to be a report.

questions.prompt: What does session memory in OpenAI's Agents SDK keep?

options.text: A board that shows which tasks of the job are done and which are still open
options.explanation: Session memory is a conversation log. It is not a status board.

options.text: The brand kit files that every role in the studio needs to read before it starts
options.explanation: Sessions store conversation history, not project files.

options.text: Conversation history, which is kept across more than one agent run, like a log
options.explanation: Right. The docs say sessions maintain conversation history across multiple agent runs.
